brief.analysis: Global military budgets have hit a record with Europe rearming, a multi-year spending shift rather than a passing headline, so defense stocks' lead over the broad market rests on real fundamentals. The engine's own trend-adjusted reading confirms this: measured against defense's rising trend the ratio is barely stretched, and it disagrees with the flat-mean reading by more than the usual margin — direct evidence the mean is drifting upward. With no moving-average confirmation and a coin-flip historical hit rate, the old average is not a valid target.
brief.report_line: Short defense-versus-market fails on its own trend-adjusted signal — the ratio is only mildly rich against a rising trend driven by record global rearmament, so the reversion mean has moved and we avoid.

brief.analysis: Chips have not merely spiked versus the broad Nasdaq — the AI build-out has turned them into the market's highest-beta engine, with the big cloud spenders guiding 2026 capital budgets above $400 billion versus roughly $230 billion in 2024. The old five-year average implies chips would have to fall about 66% relative to the index to 'revert,' which assumes a world that no longer exists; the average itself has moved up. This is a broken relationship, not a stretched rubber band, and the signal is still early and unconfirmed.
brief.report_line: Short semiconductors-versus-Nasdaq screens as extreme, but the AI capital-spending boom has permanently reset the relationship, so the reversion target is a statistical trap — avoid.

brief.analysis: The strongest case against a full snap-back is that record central-bank gold buying looks like a lasting shift in who owns gold, not a temporary spike, which can hold gold's price up versus stocks for years. That said, the trade has already done most of its work — the ratio has fallen back to its recent trading range and is only mildly stretched now — so the easy reversion is behind us; pushing on toward the old five-year average (another 12% lower) is where you'd be fighting that structural gold bid. Take the position but size it down.
brief.report_line: Short gold-versus-stocks: the overshoot has largely reverted so we hold a reduced position, but structural central-bank gold demand caps how far this can fall and argues against chasing the old five-year average.

brief.analysis: Silver has its own structural demand story — solar panels, electric vehicles and AI hardware — plus a supply squeeze, and many forecasters expect silver to keep gaining on gold, which is the opposite of what this short needs. Working in the trade's favor, the wild overshoot has already cooled sharply from its peak and the ratio has hit its medium-term average, so a partial reversion is credible. Trade it small; do not expect it to travel all the way back to the old five-year average with the metal in a bull market.
brief.report_line: Short silver-versus-gold after its record spike is tradeable in reduced size, but silver's structural industrial and supply story means the deeper reversion target may never print.

brief.analysis: Metals and miners have roughly doubled the S&P this year on a genuine rotation into materials plus copper, silver and tariff tailwinds, so part of this lead is a real commodity cycle, not just froth. Offsetting that, the sharpest overshoot has already reverted, the ratio has reached its medium-term average and the short-term trend has rolled over. The catch is a very thin track record for this setup, so treat a bounce toward the old five-year average as the fight it is and keep size modest.
brief.report_line: Short metals-and-mining-versus-market has cooled off its extreme and is tradeable small, but a live commodity up-cycle and a thin historical sample argue against sizing up toward the old average.
